newsitem.title: CHINA: China futures firm executive kills self -newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China futures firm executive kills self -newspaper.

text.p: A former executive of a commodity futures firm in Shanghai has committed suicide after suffering huge trading losses, Hong Kong's Beijing-backed Wen Wei Po newspaper said on Friday.
It was the first suicide case of its type after China revived futures trading, the report said.

Song Sucheng, former general manager of Shanghai Huanghai Futures Co, jumped to his death early on Thursday from the 15th floor of an 18-storey building along the Suzhou river in the central part of Shanghai, said the newspaper, mouthpiece of the Communist Party in Hong Kong.
Huanghai Futures Co officials said they had no information about Song. Police could not immediately be reached for comment.

The newspaper said Song lost a huge unspecified amount of money in futures trading on the Tianjian Commodity Futures Exchange, and had been warned by the securities and futures watchdog body, the China Securities Regulatory Commission.
The newspaper did not give details of when the losses occurred.
One Shanghai trader told Reuters Song lost about 100 million yuan ($12 million) in red bean futures trading on the Tianjin Exchange.
The Huanghai Futures Co was one of the first futures companies set up in China since curbs on such trading were eased in the early 1990s, the newspaper said.
It has registered capital of 10 milllion yuan.
